claims.text: An active learning-based machine learning framework using compositional descriptors can rapidly identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA compositions.
The proposed active learning framework will outperform traditional simulation-heavy alloy-design approaches.
The relevant refractory multi-principal-element alloy system has a vast composition space.
The active learning framework can be trained using existing experimental and simulation datasets.
Mixing entropy, atomic-size differences, and valence-electron concentration are suitable compositional descriptors for the framework.
The selected compositional descriptors capture indicators of short-range order.
The selected compositional descriptors capture indicators of phase stability.
Historical data allow the active learning model to correlate compositional features with strength, ductility, and density.
The learned correlations enable efficient prediction of candidate compositions from a large design space.
Model-selected compositions will exhibit enhanced mechanical properties after synthesis.
Model-selected compositions will have reduced weight relative to alloys derived from conventional simulation approaches.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and atomistic simulation methods are computationally intensive.
Traditional methods require trial-and-error exploration of the alloy composition space.
The approach may be less effective when training datasets inadequately represent the composition space.
The approach may be less effective when unforeseen physical phenomena occur in unexplored composition regions.
Prediction success depends on training-data quality, training-data coverage, and descriptor relevance.
